claims.claim: A value proposition is a summary describing benefits customers can expect from a particular product or service.
Customer value can include doing something more easily, more quickly, or at lower cost than before; a feature list is not itself a statement of those benefits.
A jobs-to-be-done framing treats a job as what an individual wants to accomplish in a given circumstance and can include functional, social, and emotional dimensions.
Competitive analysis examines potential customers, competitors, and alternatives to help identify a competitive edge; customer-relevant differentiation is not established by novelty alone.

Existing market sources are useful for general, quantitative questions but may not be specific to a particular audience, while direct research can offer more nuance about a specific business or customer.
A value proposition by itself is not evidence that customers will choose an offering, that product-market fit exists, or that a venture will succeed.
